An Act to provide for the regulation of the export, import and transit of hazardous waste, and for related purposes

section.heading: Short title

content.p: This Act may be cited as the Hazardous Waste (Regulation of Exports and Imports) Act 1989.

section.heading: Commencement

content.p: Subject to subsection (2), this Act commences on a day to be fixed by Proclamation.

If this Act does not commence under subsection (1) within the period of 6 months beginning on the day on which it receives the Royal Assent, it commences on the first day after the end of that period.

section.heading: Object and aims

content.p: Object

The object of this Act is to regulate the export, import and transit of hazardous waste to ensure that exported, imported or transited waste is managed in an environmentally sound manner so that human beings and the environment, both within and outside Australia, are protected from the harmful effects of the waste.
Aims
The aims of this Act are:
to give effect to the Basel Convention on the Control of Transboundary Movements of Hazardous Wastes and their Disposal; and
to give effect to agreements and arrangements of the kind mentioned in Article 11 of that Convention.

section.heading: Exports and transits to foreign countries—extended meaning of hazardous waste

content.p: When this section has effect
This section has effect for the purposes of the application of this Act:
to the export or proposed export of a substance or object to a particular foreign country; or
to, or to the carrying out of, a transit proposal that involves the export of a substance or object to a particular foreign country.
Declaration extending the meaning of hazardous waste—classification under foreign laws
If:
the foreign country is a party to the Basel Convention; and
the CEO is satisfied that, under a law of that country that gives effect to the Basel Convention, a particular substance or object is, in particular circumstances, classified as hazardous waste; and
apart from this section, the waste is not hazardous waste;
the CEO must, by writing, declare that that substance or object is, in those circumstances, hazardous waste for those purposes.
Declaration extending the meaning of hazardous waste—waste collected from households
If:
the CEO is satisfied that the foreign country classifies particular waste collected from households as hazardous waste; and
apart from this section, the waste is not hazardous waste;
the CEO must, by writing, declare that that waste is hazardous waste for those purposes.
Declaration has effect accordingly
A declaration under this section has effect accordingly.

the CEO must revoke the declaration.

section.heading: Transit proposals

content.p: (1) This section sets out the proposals that are transit proposals for the purposes of this Act.
Note: Australia does not include Australian waters (see section 4).
Transit proposal
A proposal:
to bring hazardous waste into Australia (whether or not by way of import); and
to take the waste out of Australia within 30 days;
is a transit proposal so long as it is not proposed to dispose of the waste in Australia.
Extension of time for carrying out proposal

If the CEO is satisfied that there are special circumstances relating to a particular proposal, the CEO may, by writing, declare that subsection (2) applies to the proposal as if a reference in that subsection to 30 days were a reference to such longer period as is specified in the declaration.
Declaration has effect accordingly
The declaration has effect accordingly.
Notification of decision
If the CEO decides to make, or not to make, a declaration under this section about a person’s proposal, the CEO must give the person a written notification of the decision.
Gazettal of declaration
(6) If the CEO makes a declaration under this section, the CEO must arrange for a copy of the declaration to be published in the Gazette.
Deemed export

For the purposes of this Act, if hazardous waste is taken out of Australia in the course of carrying out a transit proposal, the taking of the waste out of Australia is to be treated as the export of the waste.
Definitions
In this section:
dispose of does not include store.

take waste out of Australia means take waste out of Australia for the purpose of importing the waste into a foreign country (whether or not the waste will be transported through any other foreign countries).

section.heading: Treatment of colonies etc.

content.p: When colony etc. is a party to the Basel Convention
For the purposes of this Act, if:
a territory is covered by either of the following subparagraphs:
a colony, overseas territory, overseas province or protectorate of a foreign country;
a territory outside Australia, where a foreign country is to any extent responsible for the international relations of the territory; and
the foreign country is a party to the Basel Convention; and
the territory is not specified in the regulations;
the territory is taken to be a party to the Basel Convention.
Competent authority of colony etc.
For the purposes of this Act, if a territory is covered by any of the following paragraphs:
a colony, overseas territory, overseas province or protectorate of a foreign country; or
a territory outside Australia, where a foreign country is to any extent responsible for the international relations of the territory; or
a territory outside Australia that is to some extent self-governing, but that is not recognised as an independent sovereign state by Australia;
a person or organisation that officially represents the territory is taken to be a competent authority of the territory.
Subsection (2) has effect despite the definition of competent authority
(3) Subsection (2) has effect despite anything in the definition of competent authority in section 4.

section.heading: Environmentally sound management of hazardous waste

content.p: A reference in this Act to the environmentally sound management of hazardous waste is a reference to taking all practicable steps to ensure that the waste is managed in a manner that will protect human health, and the environment, against the adverse effects that may result from the waste.

section.heading: Article 11 arrangements—substances taken to be hazardous waste

content.p: This section has effect for the purposes of the application of this Act:
to the import or proposed import of a substance or object from a particular foreign country; or
to the export or proposed export of a substance or object to a particular foreign country; or
to, or to the carrying out of, a transit proposal that involves the export of a substance or object to a particular foreign country.
If:
the country is a party to an Article 11 arrangement; and
the substance or object is subject to notification or control under the arrangement; and
apart from this section, the substance or object is not hazardous waste;
the substance or object is taken to be hazardous waste for those purposes.

section.heading: Article 11 arrangements—substances not classified as hazardous waste

content.p: This section has effect for the purposes of the application of this Act:
to the import or proposed import of a substance or object from a particular foreign country; or
to the export or proposed export of a substance or object to a particular foreign country; or
to, or to the carrying out of, a transit proposal that involves the export of a substance or object to a particular foreign country.
If:
the country is a party to an Article 11 arrangement; and
the arrangement expressly provides that the substance or object is not subject to notification or control under the arrangement;
the substance or object is taken not to be hazardous waste for those purposes.

section.heading: Failure to comply with permit condition when required is breach of condition

content.p: For the purposes of this Act, if:
under subsection 22(2) or 26(2), the CEO specifies the day on or before which a permit condition relating to a Basel permit is to be complied with; and
the condition is not complied with on or before that day;
the holder of the permit is to be taken to have breached the condition at the end of that day.
For the purposes of this Act, if:
under a set of Article 11 regulations, the CEO specifies the day on or before which a permit condition relating to a special permit is to be complied with; and
the condition is not complied with on or before that day;
the holder of the permit is taken to have breached that condition at the end of that day.

section.heading: Extension to external Territories

content.p: This Act, and the Regulatory Powers Act to the extent that it applies in relation to a provision of this Act, extend to every external Territory.

section.heading: Extraterritorial operation

content.p: This Act and Regulatory Powers Act generally apply within and outside of Australian jurisdiction
Subject to this section, this Act, and the Regulatory Powers Act as it applies in relation to this Act, extend to acts, omissions, matters and things outside of Australian jurisdiction.
Note: Some searchable places will be outside of Australian jurisdiction.
Regulatory provisions applying outside of Australian jurisdiction apply only to Australian entities

Subject to subsections (4) and (5), to the extent that a provision of this Act, or a provision of the Regulatory Powers Act as it applies in relation to this Act, has effect in relation to anywhere outside of Australian jurisdiction, that provision applies only in relation to relevant Australian entities.
Regulatory provisions apply to all entities etc. in Australian jurisdiction

Subject to subsection (4), to the extent that a provision of this Act, or a provision of the Regulatory Powers Act as it applies in relation to this Act, has effect in relation to Australian jurisdiction, that provision applies in relation to:
all relevant persons including foreign persons; and
all relevant searchable places in that jurisdiction, including any owned or occupied by foreign persons.
This Act and the Regulatory Powers Act have effect subject to international law obligations
This Act, and the Regulatory Powers Act as it applies in relation to this Act, have effect subject to:
the obligations of Australia under international law, including obligations under any international agreement binding on Australia; and
any law of the Commonwealth giving effect to such an agreement.

The exercise in a foreign country of a power under this Act, or the Regulatory Powers Act as it applies in relation to this Act, is subject to the consent of the foreign country, if such consent is required under international law (including requirements under any international agreement binding on Australia).
Definitions
In this section:
Australian entity means:
an Australian citizen; or
an individual who is a resident of Australia; or
a body corporate established by or under a law of the Commonwealth, of a State or of a Territory; or
an Australian aircraft; or
an Australian vessel.
foreign person means a person other than:
an Australian citizen; or
an individual who is a resident of Australia; or
a body corporate established by or under a law of the Commonwealth, of a State or of a Territory.

section.heading: Geographical application of offences

content.p: Division 14 (standard geographical jurisdiction) of the Criminal Code does not apply in relation to an offence against this Act.
Note: The extended geographical application that section 9A gives to this Act applies to the offences and civil penalty provisions of this Act.

section.heading: Act binds Crown

content.p: This Act binds the Crown in right of the Commonwealth, of each of the States, of the Australian Capital Territory and of the Northern Territory.

section.heading: Application of the Criminal Code

content.p: Chapter 2 (other than Part 2.5 and Division 14) of the Criminal Code applies to all offences against this Act.
Note: Chapter 2 of the Criminal Code sets out the general principles of criminal responsibility.

section.heading: Relationship between Act and other Commonwealth laws

content.p: This Act is in addition to, and not in derogation of or substitution for, the Customs Act 1901, the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999 or any other law of the Commonwealth, whether enacted before or after the commencement of this Act.

part.heading: Import permits, export permits and transit permits

section.heading: Applications for import permits

content.p: A person who has one or more import proposals in relation to hazardous waste may apply to the CEO for a permit authorising the import of the waste.
The application must:
be in the form approved by the CEO; and
set out, or be accompanied by, such information relating to the proposals as is required by the form.
The application may deal with 2 or more import proposals in relation to hazardous waste only if:
the following matters are common to each proposal:
the physical and chemical characteristics of the waste;
the route over which the waste is to be transported;
the sender of the waste; and
the proposals constitute a regular pattern; and
the proposals will all be carried out within 12 months of each other.

section.heading: Applications for export permits

content.p: A person who has one or more export proposals in relation to hazardous waste may apply to the CEO for a permit authorising the export of the waste.
The application must:
be in the form approved by the CEO; and
set out, or be accompanied by, such information relating to the proposals as is required by the form.
The application may deal with 2 or more export proposals in relation to hazardous waste only if:
the following matters are common to each proposal:
the physical and chemical characteristics of the waste;
the route over which the waste is to be transported;
the recipient of the waste; and
the proposals constitute a regular pattern; and
the proposals will all be carried out within 12 months of each other.

section.heading: Applications for transit permits

content.p: A person who has one or more transit proposals in relation to hazardous waste may apply to the CEO for a permit to carry out the proposals.

Note: If a transit proposal is in connection with the movement of hazardous waste from one OECD country to another OECD country, a transit permit may not be required for that proposal: see subsection 33G(1).
The application must:
be in the form approved by the CEO; and
set out, or be accompanied by, such information relating to the proposals as is required by the form.
The application may deal with 2 or more transit proposals in relation to hazardous waste only if:
the following matters are common to each proposal:
the physical and chemical characteristics of the waste;
the route over which the waste is to be transported;
the sender and recipient of the waste; and
the proposals constitute a regular pattern; and
the proposals will all be carried out within 12 months of each other.

section.heading: Basel permit or special permit

content.p: Statement in application
An application under section 12, 13 or 13A must state that the applicant is applying for:
a Basel permit; or
a special permit under a specified set of Article 11 regulations;
but not both.
Application specifying Basel permit—adjustment of application
Note 1: If the applicant has applied for a Basel permit, the application is to be dealt with in accordance with Division 3.
Note 2: If the applicant has applied for a special permit under a particular set of Article 11 regulations, the application is to be dealt with in accordance with that set of regulations.
If:
an application under section 12, 13 or 13A states that the applicant is applying for a Basel permit; and
the CEO is satisfied that there are special circumstances relating to the application;

the CEO may, by writing, determine that this Act has effect as if the applicant had applied instead for the corresponding type of special permit under a set of Article 11 regulations specified in the determination.
Application specifying special permit—adjustment of application
If:
an application under section 12, 13 or 13A states that the applicant is applying for a special permit under a particular set of Article 11 regulations; and
the CEO is satisfied that there are special circumstances relating to the application;
the CEO may, by writing:
determine that this Act has effect as if the applicant had applied instead for the corresponding type of Basel permit; or
determine that this Act has effect as if the applicant had applied instead for the corresponding type of special permit under another set of Article 11 regulations specified in the determination.
Determination has effect accordingly
A determination under this section has effect accordingly.
Applicant to be given copy of determination
As soon as practicable after the CEO makes a determination under this section, the CEO must give the applicant a copy of the determination.

division.heading: Special permits under a set of Article 11 regulations

section.heading: Regulations may give effect to Article 11 arrangements

content.p: The regulations may provide for and in relation to:
giving effect to an Article 11 arrangement; and
giving effect to an amendment of an Article 11 arrangement.

Regulations made for the purposes of this section may be expressed to take effect on the day the arrangement or amendment enters into force, or comes into effect, for Australia (but must not be expressed to take effect before then).
(2A) As soon as practicable after the arrangement or amendment enters into force, or comes into effect, for Australia, the Minister must publish a notice in the Gazette giving details of that fact.

(3) Regulations made for the purposes of this section that give effect to a particular Article 11 arrangement (including regulations that give effect to an amendment of the Article 11 arrangement) are to be known as a set of Article 11 regulations.

section.heading: Contents of a set of Article 11 regulations

content.p: Each set of Article 11 regulations may:
specify the kinds of import proposals, export proposals and transit proposals that are within the scope of that set of regulations; and
provide for the granting of permits by the CEO authorising the import of hazardous waste, where the permit relates to an import proposal within the scope of that set of regulations; and
provide for the granting of permits by the CEO authorising the export of hazardous waste, where the permit relates to an export proposal within the scope of that set of regulations; and
provide for the granting of permits by the CEO authorising the carrying out of transit proposals within the scope of that set of regulations.
Note 1: A permit covered by paragraph (1)(b) is known as a special import permit—see the definition in section 4.
Note 2: A permit covered by paragraph (1)(c) is known as a special export permit—see the definition in section 4.
Note 3: A permit covered by paragraph (1)(d) is known as a special transit permit—see the definition in section 4.
A set of Article 11 regulations may provide for:
conditions of special permits; and
the revocation, surrender and variation of special permits.
This section does not, by implication, limit section 13C.

section.heading: Special permit may be granted under a set of Article 11 regulations only if corresponding requirements of other sets of Article 11 regulations have been met

content.p: Import
If:
a person applies for a special import permit in relation to an import proposal that is within the scope of a particular set of Article 11 regulations; and
the proposal is within the scope of another set of Article 11 regulations;

the CEO must not grant the permit unless the CEO is satisfied that the corresponding requirements of the other set of regulations have been met in relation to the proposal. For this purpose, a corresponding requirement of a particular set of Article 11 regulations is a requirement under that set of regulations:
that must be met before granting a special import permit under that set of regulations; and
that is declared by the regulations to be a corresponding requirement for the purposes of this subsection.

Subsection (1) does not prevent the set of Article 11 regulations mentioned in paragraph (1)(a) from setting out other requirements that must be met before granting a special import permit under that set of regulations.
Export
If:
a person applies for a special export permit in relation to an export proposal that is within the scope of a particular set of Article 11 regulations; and
the proposal is within the scope of another set of Article 11 regulations;

the CEO must not grant the permit unless the CEO is satisfied that the corresponding requirements of the other set of regulations have been met in relation to the proposal. For this purpose, a corresponding requirement of a particular set of Article 11 regulations is:

a requirement under that set of regulations to obtain the consent (whether actual or constructive) of an authority of a foreign country before granting a special export permit under that set of regulations authorising the export of hazardous waste to that country; or
another requirement under that set of regulations:
that must be met before granting a special export permit under that set of regulations; and
that is declared by the regulations to be a corresponding requirement for the purposes of this subsection.

Subsection (3) does not prevent the set of Article 11 regulations mentioned in paragraph (3)(a) from setting out other requirements that must be met before granting a special export permit under that set of regulations.
Transit
If:
a person applies for a special transit permit in relation to a transit proposal that is within the scope of a particular set of Article 11 regulations; and
the proposal is within the scope of another set of Article 11 regulations;

the CEO must not grant the permit unless the CEO is satisfied that the corresponding requirements of the other set of regulations have been met in relation to the proposal. For this purpose, a corresponding requirement of a particular set of Article 11 regulations is:

a requirement under that set of regulations to obtain the consent (whether actual or constructive) of an authority of a foreign country before granting a special transit permit under that set of regulations authorising the carrying out of a transit proposal that involves the export of hazardous waste to that country; or
another requirement under that set of regulations:
that must be met before granting a special transit permit under that set of regulations; and
that is declared by the regulations to be a corresponding requirement for the purposes of this subsection.

Subsection (5) does not prevent the set of Article 11 regulations mentioned in paragraph (5)(a) from setting out other requirements that must be met before granting a special transit permit under that set of regulations.

section.heading: Special permit—waste not to be brought into Antarctica

content.p: The CEO must not grant a special permit if the CEO is satisfied that the grant could result in hazardous waste being brought into Antarctica.

section.heading: Variation of applications for Basel permits

content.p: An applicant for a Basel permit may, at any time before the CEO has decided whether to grant the permit, give the CEO a notice stating that the permit application is varied as set out in the notice.
The notice must:
be in the form approved by the CEO; and
set out, or be accompanied by, such information relating to the variation as is required by the form.
If the CEO receives a notice under subsection (1) from the applicant:
the application is to be taken to have been varied in accordance with the notice; and
the application, as varied, is to be taken to have been received by the CEO on the day on which the CEO received the notice.

section.heading: CEO may request further information about an application

content.p: Within 60 days after the day of receiving an application for a Basel permit, the CEO may request the applicant to provide further information in writing to deal with the application.
If the CEO makes such a request of an applicant:
the period in subsection 16(1) for the CEO to decide whether to grant the Basel permit is paused until the request is complied with; and
the application is taken to be withdrawn if the request is not complied with within 60 days after the day that the request is made.

section.heading: Acknowledgment and notification

content.p: Within 7 days after receiving an application for a Basel permit, the CEO must give the applicant a written acknowledgment of the receipt.

Within 7 days after receiving an application for a Basel import permit authorising the import of hazardous waste from a foreign country, the CEO must give the competent authority of the country a written notification of the receipt.

section.heading: Period for making decision on application for Basel permit—default period

content.p: (1) The CEO must decide whether to grant the Basel permit within 60 days starting on the day after the CEO receives the application (the decision period).
Note: This period may be paused or extended under section 15, 16A, 16B, 16C or 16D.
If the CEO has not decided whether to grant the permit by the end of the decision period, the CEO is to be taken to have decided, on the last day of that period, not to grant the permit.

section.heading: Period for making decision on application for Basel permit—extensions for Basel export permits

content.p: If the application is for a Basel export permit, then within 21 days after the day of receiving the application, the CEO must notify:
(a) the competent authority of the country to which hazardous waste is to be exported under the permit (the receiving country); and
(b) the competent authority of each country (if any) (a transit country) through which the hazardous waste is to be transported in order to export it to the receiving country;
of such information about the application as is required by regulations made for the purposes of this subsection.
If, at the end of the 46th day of the decision period, either:
the competent authority of the receiving country has neither given nor refused written consent to the grant of the permit; or
a competent authority of a transit country notified under paragraph (1)(b) has neither given nor refused written consent to the grant of the permit;
the decision period is paused until the earlier of:
the latest day such a refusal or consent is given by a competent authority covered by paragraph (a) or (b); and
12 months after the day the CEO receives the application.

If a foreign country is a party to the Basel Convention, a reference in subsection (2) to a consent given by the competent authority of the country is a reference to a consent given in accordance with Article 6 of the Basel Convention.

section.heading: Period for making decision on application for Basel permit—extensions for Basel permits

content.p: If:
the application is for a Basel permit; and
the CEO thinks that it will take more than 60 days to decide whether to grant the permit;
the CEO may extend the decision period by up to a further 60 days.
The CEO must give written notice of any extension under subsection (1) to each of the following as soon as practicable:
the applicant;
in the case of an application for a Basel import permit—the competent authority of the country from which the permit authorises the import of hazardous waste;
in the case of a Basel export permit—the following:
(i) the competent authority of the country to which the permit authorises the export of hazardous waste (the receiving country);
the competent authority of each country (if any) through which the permit authorises the hazardous waste to be transported in order to export it to the receiving country.

section.heading: Period for making decision on application for Basel permit—referrals under the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999

content.p: If, within the decision period, the proposal to grant the Basel permit is referred under Subdivision A of Division 4 of Part 11 of the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999, the decision period is paused until:
the Minister administering that Subdivision gives, under section 163 of that Act, advice on the proposed grant; or
the Minister administering that Subdivision decides, under section 161A of that Act, that that Subdivision does not apply to the referral.

Note: Under Subdivision A of Division 4 of Part 11 of the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999, persons considering whether to authorise certain actions must get advice on environmental matters from the Minister administering that Subdivision.

section.heading: Period for making decision on application for Basel permit—extension agreed with applicant

content.p: The decision period is extended if the CEO and applicant agree in writing to the extension.

section.heading: Grant of Basel import permits and Basel export permits

content.p: This section applies if the permit sought by a permit application is a Basel import permit or a Basel export permit.
Subject to this Division, the CEO must grant the permit sought by a permit application if:

the CEO is satisfied that dealing with the hazardous waste concerned in accordance with the import proposals or export proposals would be consistent with the environmentally sound management of the hazardous waste; and
in the case of a Basel export permit authorising the export of hazardous waste to a particular foreign country:
the CEO is satisfied that the competent authority of the country has given written consent to the grant of the permit; and
the CEO is satisfied that the consent was given in accordance with Article 6 of the Basel Convention; and

in the case of a Basel export permit— the CEO is satisfied that the hazardous waste will be allowed to be transported through any foreign country through which the waste is proposed to be transported; and
the CEO is satisfied that, having regard to:
the applicant’s financial viability; and
the applicant’s previous record in relation to environmental matters; and
any other relevant matters;
the applicant is a suitable person to be granted a Basel permit; and
the CEO is satisfied that the applicant has appropriate insurance; and
the CEO has taken into account any relevant public comments received in response to an invitation under paragraph 33(1)(aa) about the permit application (or any notice relating to that application).
Note: Section 18 specifies circumstances in which the applicant has appropriate insurance.
Even if the CEO is satisfied as mentioned in subsection (1), the CEO may decide under subsection (2A), (3), (4), (5) or (5A) not to grant the permit.
The CEO may decide not to grant the permit if:
the permit sought is a Basel export permit; and
having regard to the requirements of paragraph 3(b) of Article 6 of the Basel Convention, the CEO thinks that it would not be appropriate to grant the permit.
The CEO may decide not to grant the permit if the CEO thinks that it would not be in the public interest to grant the permit.
The CEO may decide not to grant the permit if the CEO thinks that:
there is another way in which the hazardous waste could be dealt with; and
dealing with the waste in the other way would not pose a significant risk of injury or damage to human beings or the environment; and
having regard to Australia’s international obligations, the waste should be dealt with in the other way rather than in accordance with the import proposals or export proposals.
The CEO may decide not to grant the permit if the permit sought is a Basel export permit and the CEO thinks that:
the hazardous waste could be disposed of safely and efficiently by using a facility in Australia; and
such a disposal would be consistent with the environmentally sound management of the waste; and

having regard to the desirability of using facilities in Australia for the disposal of hazardous waste, the waste should be disposed of by using that facility rather than in accordance with the export proposals.

The CEO may decide not to grant the permit if the applicant has previously failed to provide, or to arrange to provide, an auditor with assistance that is reasonably necessary for the conduct of an audit.
Note 1: For the requirement to provide an auditor with assistance that is reasonably necessary for the conduct of an audit, see section 54.

Note 2: The audit need not relate to a permit. Assistance may be requested in relation to any audit of operations covered by a permit, an order under Part 3, a notification given under subsection 33G(1), or other prescribed operations: see section 50.
The CEO must not grant a Basel export permit or a Basel import permit if the CEO is satisfied that the grant could result in hazardous waste being brought into Antarctica.
The CEO must not grant a Basel export permit authorising the export of hazardous waste to a foreign country that is not a party to the Basel Convention.
The CEO must not grant a Basel import permit authorising the import of hazardous waste from a foreign country that is not a party to the Basel Convention.

section.heading: Grant of transit permits

content.p: This section applies if the permit sought by a permit application is a Basel transit permit.
The CEO must grant the permit sought by a permit application if:
the CEO is satisfied that carrying out the transit proposals will not pose a significant risk of injury or damage to human beings or the environment; and
the CEO is satisfied that, having regard to:
the applicant’s financial viability; and
the applicant’s previous record in relation to environmental matters; and
any other relevant matters;
the applicant is a suitable person to be granted a Basel transit permit; and
the CEO is satisfied that the applicant has appropriate insurance; and
the CEO has taken into account any relevant public comments received in response to an invitation under paragraph 33(1)(aa) about the permit application (or any notice relating to that application).
Note: Section 18 specifies circumstances in which the applicant has appropriate insurance.
Subsection (2) has effect subject to this Division.
The CEO may decide not to grant the permit if the CEO thinks that it would not be in the public interest to grant it.

The CEO may decide not to grant the permit if the applicant has previously failed to provide, or to arrange to provide, an auditor with assistance that is reasonably necessary for the conduct of an audit.
Note 1: For the requirement to provide an auditor with assistance that is reasonably necessary for the conduct of an audit, see section 54.

Note 2: The audit need not relate to a permit. Assistance may be requested in relation to any audit of operations covered by a permit, an order under Part 3, a notification given under subsection 33G(1), or other prescribed operations: see section 50.
The CEO must not grant the permit if the CEO is satisfied that carrying out the transit proposals could result in hazardous waste being brought into Antarctica.

section.heading: Determination of whether applicant has appropriate insurance

content.p: An applicant for a Basel permit has appropriate insurance for the purposes of section 17 or 17A if:
the applicant is reasonably insured against risks that might arise in relation to the hazardous waste concerned if the permit were granted; or

the applicant, whether because of arrangements made by the applicant or otherwise, will be able to discharge any liability of the applicant that might arise in relation to the hazardous waste concerned if the permit were granted.

section.heading: Export permits for final disposal may be granted only in exceptional circumstances

content.p: The CEO must not grant a Basel export permit authorising the export of hazardous waste if the applicant proposes that the hazardous waste will be disposed of by a method that is within the scope of Section A of Annex IV to the Basel Convention.
Despite subsection (1), the CEO may grant a Basel export permit in the circumstances described in that subsection if the CEO is satisfied that there are exceptional circumstances.
Subsection (2) does not apply if the CEO is satisfied that carrying out the export proposals would be inconsistent with the environmentally sound management of the hazardous waste.
In deciding whether there are exceptional circumstances for the purposes of subsection (2), the CEO must have regard to the following:
whether there will be a significant risk of injury or damage to human beings or the environment if the CEO decides not to grant the permit;
whether the waste is needed for research into improving the management of hazardous waste;
whether the waste is needed for testing for the purposes of improving the management of hazardous waste;
matters prescribed for the purposes of this paragraph.

section.heading: Basel permit may be granted only if the corresponding requirements of Article 11 regulations have been met

content.p: Import
If:
a person applies for a Basel import permit in relation to an import proposal; and
the proposal is within the scope of a particular set of Article 11 regulations;

the CEO must not grant the permit unless the CEO is satisfied that the corresponding requirements of that set of regulations have been met in relation to the proposal. For this purpose, a corresponding requirement of a particular set of Article 11 regulations is a requirement under that set of regulations:
that must be met before granting a special import permit under that set of regulations; and
that is declared by the regulations to be a corresponding requirement for the purposes of this subsection.
Export
If:
a person applies for a Basel export permit in relation to an export proposal; and
the proposal is within the scope of a particular set of Article 11 regulations;

the CEO must not grant the permit unless the CEO is satisfied that the corresponding requirements of that set of regulations have been met in relation to the proposal. For this purpose, a corresponding requirement of a particular set of Article 11 regulations is:

a requirement under that set of regulations to obtain the consent (whether actual or constructive) of an authority of a foreign country before granting a special export permit under that set of regulations authorising the export of hazardous waste to that country; or
another requirement under that set of regulations:
that must be met before granting a special export permit under that set of regulations; and
that is declared by the regulations to be a corresponding requirement for the purposes of this subsection.
Transit
If:
a person applies for a Basel transit permit in relation to a transit proposal; and
the proposal is within the scope of a particular set of Article 11 regulations;

the CEO must not grant the permit unless the CEO is satisfied that the corresponding requirements of that set of regulations have been met in relation to the proposal. For this purpose, a corresponding requirement of a particular set of Article 11 regulations is:

a requirement under that set of regulations to obtain the consent (whether actual or constructive) of an authority of a foreign country before granting a special transit permit under that set of regulations authorising the carrying out of a transit proposal that involves the export of hazardous waste to that country; or
another requirement under that set of regulations:
that must be met before granting a special transit permit under that set of regulations; and
that is declared by the regulations to be a corresponding requirement for the purposes of this subsection.

section.heading: Applicants to be notified of decisions

content.p: If the CEO decides to grant a Basel permit, the CEO must give the permit to the applicant as soon as practicable after making the decision.
If the CEO decides not to grant a Basel permit, the CEO must give the applicant a written statement setting out the decision and the reasons for it as soon as practicable after making the decision.
A contravention of this section in relation to a decision does not affect the validity of the decision.

section.heading: Foreign countries to be notified of decision about grant of import permit

content.p: As soon as practicable after the CEO makes a decision to grant, or not to grant, a Basel import permit authorising the import of hazardous waste from a particular foreign country, the CEO must give the competent authority of the country a written notification of the decision.
A contravention of this section in relation to a decision does not affect the validity of the decision.

section.heading: Matters to be specified in Basel import permits

content.p: A Basel import permit must specify particulars of:
the kind of hazardous waste to be imported; and
the quantity of hazardous waste to be imported; and
the method of transport by which the hazardous waste is to be imported; and
the time at which, or period during which, the hazardous waste is to be imported; and
the place to which the hazardous waste is to be imported; and
the way in which the hazardous waste is to be dealt with after the import; and
if the hazardous waste is to be disposed of after the import—the facility to be used in the disposal and the process (if any) involved in the disposal.
A Basel import permit may also include conditions under section 22 and such other information as the CEO considers appropriate.

section.heading: Matters to be specified in Basel export permits

content.p: A Basel export permit must specify particulars of:
the kind of hazardous waste to be exported; and
the quantity of hazardous waste to be exported; and
the method of transport by which the hazardous waste is to be exported; and
the time at which, or period during which, the hazardous waste is to be exported; and
the way in which the hazardous waste is to be dealt with after the export; and
if the hazardous waste is to be disposed of after the export—the facility to be used in the disposal and the process (if any) involved in the disposal.
A Basel export permit may also include conditions under section 22 and such other information as the CEO considers appropriate.

section.heading: Matters to be specified in Basel transit permits

content.p: A Basel transit permit must specify particulars of the transit proposals concerned.
A Basel transit permit may also include conditions under section 22 and such other information as the CEO considers appropriate.

section.heading: Basel permits may be granted subject to conditions

content.p: The CEO may grant a Basel permit subject to conditions specified in the permit.
The CEO may specify in the Basel permit the day on or before which the holder of the permit is to comply with a condition.
A Basel transit permit must be granted subject to such conditions as the CEO considers necessary or desirable for the purposes of ensuring that the transit proposals are carried out.
A Basel permit may be granted subject to a condition relating to the giving of:
one or more guarantees; or
one or more security deposits;
in respect of compliance by the permit holder with the permit holder’s obligations under, or arising out of, this Act.
The following are examples of cases where a guarantee or a security deposit might be given:
a holding company gives the CEO a guarantee that a subsidiary of the holding company will pay any amounts owed by the subsidiary under subsection 38B(2);
a person gives the CEO a security deposit in respect of compliance by the person with the person’s obligations to pay amounts owing under subsection 38B(2).
Subsections (2A) and (2B) do not, by implication, limit subsection (1).
Note 1: Another example of a condition is one that includes a day on or before which it needs to be complied with.
Note 2: The condition could be imposed under this section or under Division 4 as a variation of the permit.

A condition is not to be taken to be intended to exclude the operation of a State or Territory law unless an intention to exclude State or Territory laws, or to exclude the particular State or Territory law, is expressed in the permit.

division.heading: Revocation, surrender and variation of Basel permits

content.p: Subdivision A—Revoking Basel permits

section.heading: Revoking Basel permits—grounds

content.p: The CEO may, in writing, decide to revoke a Basel permit if the CEO is satisfied that:
the holder of the permit:
gave the CEO false, misleading or incomplete information; and
when doing so, failed to give the CEO an explanation for doing so, or failed to give the CEO the correct or complete information if the person was reasonably able to have done so; or
the holder of the permit:
is failing, or has failed, to comply with a condition to which the permit is subject; or
is failing, or has failed, to comply with a provision of this Act relating to the permit; or
is failing, or has failed after the granting of the permit, to provide or to arrange to provide an auditor with assistance that is reasonably necessary for the conduct of an audit; or
after considering information that was not considered when granting the permit, the permit would not be granted if the CEO were now asked to grant it; or
after considering information that was not considered when granting the permit, the revocation is necessary to prevent or lessen a threat of serious harm to human health or the environment; or
a ground prescribed by the regulations for the purposes of this paragraph is satisfied for the holder and the permit.
Note 1: For the requirement to provide an auditor with assistance that is reasonably necessary for the conduct of an audit, see section 54.

Note 2: The audit need not relate to the permit. Assistance may be requested in relation to any audit of operations covered by a permit, an order under Part 3, a notification given under subsection 33G(1), or other prescribed operations: see section 50.

However, a revocation of a Basel permit only applies to an import, export or the carrying out of a transit proposal authorised by the permit if the import, export or the carrying out of the transit proposal has yet to begin.

Note 1: This subsection means that a Basel permit that authorises 2 or more imports or exports of hazardous waste, or the carrying out of 2 or more transit proposals, only applies to an import or export, or the carrying out of a transit proposal, that has not begun at the time of the revocation.

Note 2: This subsection also means a Basel permit cannot be revoked if it only authorises a single import or export that has already begun or the carrying out of a single transit proposal that has already begun.

section.heading: Revoking Basel permits—notice of proposed revocation

content.p: Despite subsection 24(1), the CEO must not revoke a Basel permit under that subsection unless:
the CEO has given a written notice to the holder of the permit in accordance with subsection (2) of this section; and
the CEO has taken into account any information given, within 14 days after the day the notice is given to the permit holder, to the CEO in response to the notice.
A notice under paragraph (1)(a) must:
specify the proposed revocation of the permit; and
specify the grounds for the proposed revocation; and
invite the holder of the permit to give the CEO, within 14 days after the day the notice is given, a written statement showing cause why the permit should not be revoked; and
include a statement setting out the holder’s right to seek review of a decision to revoke the permit.

A notice under paragraph (1)(a) is not required if the CEO reasonably believes that the proposed revocation is necessary to prevent or lessen a serious and imminent threat to human health or the environment.

section.heading: Notice of revocation

content.p: If the CEO decides under subsection 24(1) to revoke a Basel permit, the CEO must give the holder of the permit a written notice stating the following:
that the permit is to be revoked;
the reasons for the revocation;
the day the revocation is to take effect (which must not be before the day the notice is given to the holder);
information about the holder’s right to seek review of the decision.

(2) If the holder of the permit was given a notice (a show cause notice) under paragraph 24A(1)(a) that included the invitation referred to in paragraph 24A(2)(c), the revocation must not take effect before the end of 14 days after the day the show cause notice was given.

section.heading: Exhaustive statement of natural justice hearing rule

content.p: This Subdivision is taken to be an exhaustive statement of the requirements of the natural justice hearing rule in relation to the matters it deals with.
Subdivision B—Surrendering Basel permits

section.heading: Surrender of Basel permits

content.p: Subject to this section, the holder of a Basel permit may, at any time, surrender the permit by:
returning the permit to the CEO; and
giving the CEO written notice that the permit is surrendered.
If the permit is a Basel import permit, the permit may not be surrendered after any import authorised by the permit has begun.
If the permit is a Basel export permit, the permit may not be surrendered after any export authorised by the permit has begun.
If the permit is a Basel transit permit, the permit may not be surrendered after the carrying out of any transit proposal authorised by the permit has begun.
The surrender of the permit takes effect on the day on which subsection (1) is satisfied.
Subdivision C—Varying Basel permits: on application

section.heading: Varying Basel permits on application

content.p: The CEO may, on application by the holder of a Basel permit, vary the permit if:
the CEO is satisfied that, if the CEO were asked to grant the Basel permit (as proposed to be varied), the CEO would decide to grant the permit; and
the CEO has taken into account any relevant public comments received in response to an invitation under paragraph 33(1)(aa) about the application.
Note: Examples of a variation include varying or revoking a permit condition.
The application must:
be in the form approved by the CEO; and
set out, or be accompanied by, such information in relation to the proposed variation as is required by the form.
The CEO must give the applicant written notice of having received an application within 7 days after the day of receiving it.

section.heading: CEO may request further information about an application

content.p: Within 60 days after the day of receiving the application, the CEO may request the applicant to provide further information in writing to deal with the application.
If the CEO makes such a request of an applicant:
the period in subsection 26B(1) for the CEO to decide whether to make the variation is paused until the request is complied with; and
the application is taken to be withdrawn if the request is not complied with within 60 days after the day the request is made.

section.heading: Period for making a decision on an application—default period

content.p: (1) The CEO must decide whether to make the variation within the period of 60 days starting on the day after the CEO receives the application (the decision period).
Note: This period may be paused or extended under section 26A, 26C, 26D, 26E or 26F.
If the CEO does not decide whether to make the variation by the end of the decision period, the CEO is to be taken to have decided, on the last day of that period, not to make the variation.

section.heading: Period for making a decision on an application—extensions for Basel export permits

content.p: If the application is for a variation of a Basel export permit, then within 21 days after the day of receiving the application, the CEO must notify:
(a) the competent authority of the country to which hazardous waste is to be exported under the permit (the receiving country); and
(b) the competent authority of each country (if any) (a transit country) through which the hazardous waste is to be transported in order to export it to the receiving country;
of such information about the application as is required by regulations made for the purposes of this subsection.
If, at the end of the 46th day of the decision period, either:
the competent authority of the receiving country has neither given nor refused written consent to the variation; or
a competent authority of a transit country notified under paragraph (1)(b) has neither given nor refused written consent to the variation;
the decision period is paused until the earlier of:
the latest day such a refusal or consent is given by a competent authority covered by paragraph (a) or (b); and
12 months after the day the CEO receives the application.

If a foreign country is a party to the Basel Convention, a reference in subsection (2) to a consent given by the competent authority of the country is a reference to a consent given in accordance with Article 6 of the Basel Convention.

section.heading: Period for making a decision on an application—extensions for Basel permits

content.p: If:
the application is for a variation of a Basel permit; and
the CEO thinks that it will take more than 60 days to decide whether to make the variation;
the CEO may extend the decision period by up to a further 60 days.
The CEO must give written notice of any extension under subsection (1) to each of the following as soon as practicable:
the applicant;
in the case of a variation of a Basel import permit—the competent authority of the country from which the permit authorises the import of hazardous waste;
in the case of a variation of a Basel export permit—the following:
(i) the competent authority of the country to which the permit authorises the export of hazardous waste (the receiving country);
the competent authority of each country (if any) through which the permit authorises the hazardous waste to be transported in order to export it to the receiving country.

section.heading: Period for making a decision on an application—referrals under the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999

content.p: If, within the decision period, the proposal to vary the Basel permit is referred under Subdivision A of Division 4 of Part 11 of the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999, the decision period is paused until:
the Minister administering that Subdivision gives, under section 163 of that Act, advice on the proposed variation; or
the Minister administering that Subdivision decides, under section 161A of that Act, that that Subdivision does not apply to the referral.

Note: Under Subdivision A of Division 4 of Part 11 of the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999, persons considering whether to authorise certain actions must get advice on environmental matters from the Minister administering that Subdivision.

section.heading: Period for making a decision on an application—extension agreed with applicant

content.p: The decision period is extended if the CEO and applicant agree in writing to the extension.

section.heading: Notice of variation

content.p: If the CEO makes a decision in relation to an application to vary a Basel permit, the CEO must give the holder of the permit a written notice stating the following:
whether the permit is to be varied;
if the decision is that the permit is to be varied—the day the variation is to take effect;
if the decision is that the permit is not to be varied:
the reasons for the decision; and
information about the holder’s right to seek review of the decision.
Subdivision D—Varying Basel permits: on CEO’s initiative

section.heading: Varying Basel permits on CEO’s initiative—grounds

content.p: The CEO may, in writing, decide to vary a Basel permit if the CEO is satisfied that:
the holder of the permit:
gave the CEO false, misleading or incomplete information; and
when doing so, failed to give the CEO an explanation for doing so, or failed to give the CEO the correct or complete information if the person was reasonably able to have done so; or
the holder of the permit:
is failing, or has failed, to comply with a condition to which the permit is subject; or
is failing, or has failed, to comply with a provision of this Act relating to the permit; or
is failing, or has failed after the granting of the permit, to provide or to arrange to provide an auditor with assistance that is reasonably necessary for the conduct of an audit; or
after considering information that was not considered when granting the permit, the variation is necessary to prevent or lessen a threat of serious harm to human health or the environment; or
a ground prescribed by the regulations for the purposes of this paragraph is satisfied for the holder and the permit.
Note 1: Examples of a variation include imposing a condition on the permit, or varying or revoking a permit condition.
Note 2: For the requirement to provide an auditor with assistance that is reasonably necessary for the conduct of an audit, see section 54.

Note 3: The audit need not relate to the permit. Assistance may be requested in relation to any audit of operations covered by a permit, an order under Part 3, a notification given under subsection 33G(1), or other prescribed operations: see section 50.

section.heading: Varying Basel permits—notice of proposed variation

content.p: Despite section 26H, the CEO must not vary a Basel permit under that section unless:
the CEO has given a written notice to the holder of the permit in accordance with subsection (2) of this section; and
the CEO has taken into account any information given, within 14 days after the day the notice is given to the permit holder, to the CEO in response to the notice.
A notice under paragraph (1)(a) must:
specify the proposed variation of the permit; and
specify the grounds for the proposed variation; and
invite the holder of the permit to give the CEO, within 14 days after the day the notice is given, a written statement showing cause why the permit should not be varied; and
include a statement setting out the holder’s right to seek review of a decision to vary the permit.

A notice under paragraph (1)(a) is not required if the CEO reasonably believes that the proposed variation is necessary to prevent or lessen a serious and imminent threat to human health or the environment.

section.heading: Notice of variation

content.p: If the CEO decides under section 26H to vary a Basel permit, the CEO must give the holder of the permit a written notice stating the following:
that the permit is to be varied;
the reasons for the variation;
the day the variation is to take effect (which must not be before the day the notice is given to the holder);

Example: A variation could impose a condition to be complied with on or after the day the variation takes effect in relation to an import that has already happened.

(2) If the holder of the permit was given a notice (a show cause notice) under paragraph 26J(1)(a) that included the invitation referred to in paragraph 26J(2)(c), the day stated under paragraph (1)(c) of this section when the variation is to take effect must not be before the end of 14 days after the day the show cause notice was given.

section.heading: Exhaustive statement of natural justice hearing rule

content.p: This Subdivision is taken to be an exhaustive statement of the requirements of the natural justice hearing rule in relation to the matters it deals with.

section.heading: Applications and notices to be accompanied by fees

content.p: The regulations may prescribe fees to be paid in relation to applications and notices given to the CEO under this Part or under a set of Article 11 regulations.
An application or notice given to the CEO under this Part or under a set of Article 11 regulations must be accompanied by the prescribed fee (if any).

If an application or notice given to the CEO under this Part or under a set of Article 11 regulations is not accompanied by the prescribed fee (if any), the application or notice is to be taken not to have been received by the CEO until the fee has been paid.

The amount or rate of a fee must be reasonably related to the expenses incurred or to be incurred by the Commonwealth in relation to the application or notice to which it relates, and must not be such as to amount to taxation.
The CEO may wholly or partly waive, or wholly or partly refund, a prescribed fee in circumstances prescribed by the regulations.
The regulations may make provision for and in relation to the indexation of prescribed fees.

section.heading: Applications to be accompanied by levy

content.p: (1) An application under section 12, 13 or 13A must be accompanied by the levy imposed by the Hazardous Waste (Regulation of Exports and Imports) Levy Act 2017.
Note: An application under section 12, 13 or 13A must be for a Basel permit or a special permit under a specified set of Article 11 regulations: see section 13B.
If the application is not accompanied by the levy, the application is taken not to have been received by the CEO until the levy has been paid.

section.heading: Publication of certain particulars on NEPA’s website

content.p: Requirement to publish information
(1) The CEO must publish on NEPA’s website particulars of:
each application and notice received by the CEO under this Part or under a set of Article 11 regulations; and

for each application or notice described in paragraph (a)—an invitation for members of the public to comment on the application or notice within 15 business days after being published under this subsection; and
each Basel permit or special permit granted; and
each decision not to grant a Basel permit or special permit; and
each revocation of a Basel permit or special permit; and
each surrender of a Basel permit or special permit; and
each variation of a Basel permit or special permit; and
each determination under section 13B.
The particulars may include the name of the person concerned.
Exception—contrary to the public interest

Subsection (1) does not apply to particular information if the CEO determines, in writing, that to publish the information would be contrary to the public interest because the publication would, or could reasonably be expected to:
endanger public safety; or
cause damage to:
the security of Australia; or
the defence of Australia; or
the international relations of Australia.
Exception—invitations for public comment
Subsection (1) does not apply to publishing an invitation described in paragraph (1)(aa) for public comment on an application or notice if the CEO is satisfied that:
the existence of exceptional circumstances means it is inappropriate to do so; or
it would not be in the public interest to do so; or
the application, or notice, is for a variation that is of a minor or technical nature.
Exception—minor or technical variations of a permit
Subsection (1) does not apply to:
a variation of a kind described in paragraph (1)(f); or
an application for such a variation;
if the variation is of a minor or technical nature.
Publishing must happen as soon as practicable after it is required
The CEO must cause a publication required by this section to be made as soon as practicable after the requirement arises.

division.heading: Regulation of import of hazardous waste

section.heading: Import of hazardous waste—basic contravention

Compliance with permit conditions
A person contravenes this subsection if:
in the course of carrying out a transit proposal, the person brings waste into Australia (whether or not by way of import); and
the waste is hazardous waste; and
the person is the holder of a transit permit authorising the person to bring the hazardous waste into Australia; and
the permit is subject to a permit condition; and
the person does an act or omits to do an act; and
the act or omission does not comply with the permit condition in relation to the transit of the hazardous waste (whether before, during or after bringing it into Australia); and
the non-compliance with the permit condition injures or damages, or is likely to injure or damage, human beings or the environment.
Note: The physical elements of an offence against subsection (5) are set out in this subsection (see section 58F).
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1), (2), (3) or (4).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 8 years or 500 penalty units, or both.
Alternative verdict
In a trial for an offence against subsection (5), the trier of fact may find the defendant not guilty of that offence, but guilty of an offence against subsection 33E(5), if:
the trier of fact is not satisfied that the defendant is guilty of the offence against subsection (5) of this section; and
the trier of fact is satisfied that the defendant is guilty of the offence against subsection 33E(5); and
the defendant has been accorded procedural fairness in relation to that finding of guilt.
Strict liability offence
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subsection (1), (2), (3) or (4).
Penalty: 60 penalty units.
Civil penalty provision
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1), (2), (3) or (4).
Civil penalty: 1,000 penalty units.

section.heading: Notice that transit permit not required

content.p: The CEO may notify a person, in writing, that the person does not require a transit permit for a transit proposal if the CEO is satisfied:
that carrying out the transit proposal is in connection with the movement of hazardous waste from one OECD country to another OECD country; and
that the hazardous waste is destined for recovery operations; and
that carrying out the transit proposal will not pose a significant risk of injury or damage to human beings or the environment; and
of any other matters prescribed by the regulations for the purposes of this paragraph; and
of any other matters the CEO considers relevant.

Even if the CEO is satisfied as mentioned in subsection (1), the CEO may decide not to give a notification under that subsection if the applicant has previously failed to provide, or to arrange to provide, an auditor with assistance that is reasonably necessary for the conduct of an audit.
Note 1: For the requirement to provide an auditor with assistance that is reasonably necessary for the conduct of an audit, see section 54.

Note 2: The audit need not relate to a notification. Assistance may be requested in relation to any audit of operations covered by a permit, an order under Part 3, a notification given under subsection 33G(1), or other prescribed operations: see section 50.
The CEO must, as soon as practicable after giving a notification under subsection (1), publish on NEPA’s website, particulars of the notification.
The CEO may, by notifying a person in writing, revoke a notification of the person under subsection (1) for a transit proposal if the CEO:
is no longer satisfied of the matters in paragraphs (1)(a) to (d) in relation to the transit proposal and the person; or

is satisfied that the person is failing, or has failed after the notice was given, to provide, or to arrange to provide, an auditor with assistance that is reasonably necessary for the conduct of an audit.
However, a revocation of a notification only applies to the carrying out of a transit proposal if the carrying out of the transit proposal has yet to begin.

division.heading: Regulation of sale of hazardous waste

section.heading: Regulation of sale of hazardous waste

content.p: A person contravenes this subsection if:
the person sells waste to a body corporate incorporated outside Australia (whether the sale occurs within or outside Australia); and
the waste is hazardous waste; and
the body corporate:
does not have a registered office in Australia; or
does not have a principal office, and at least one executive officer, in Australia; and
the person sells the waste knowing, or being reckless as to whether, the waste is to be exported by the body corporate; and
an export permit authorising the export of the waste is not in force when the sale occurs.
Note: The physical elements of an offence against subsection (3) are set out in this subsection (see section 58F).
A person contravenes this subsection if:
the person sells waste to another person who is located outside Australia; and
the waste is hazardous waste; and
the person sells the waste knowing, or being reckless as to whether, the waste is to be exported; and
an export permit authorising the export of the waste is not in force when the sale occurs.
Note: The physical elements of an offence against subsection (3) are set out in this subsection (see section 58F).
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1) or (2).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 3 years or 180 penalty units, or both.
Civil penalty provision
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1) or (2).
Civil penalty: 360 penalty units.

part.heading: Orders in relation to hazardous waste

section.heading: Orders relating to import of hazardous waste

content.p: If a person contravenes one or more of the provisions mentioned in subsection (2) in relation to hazardous waste, the CEO may, in writing, order the person to deal with the waste in a specified way.
For the purposes of subsection (1), the provisions are the following:
subsection 33A(1) (import of hazardous waste—basic contravention);
subsection 33A(2) (import in accordance with permit—basic contravention);
subsection 33A(3) (compliance with permit conditions—basic contravention);
subsection 33B(1) (import of hazardous waste—injury or damage);
subsection 33B(2) (import in accordance with permit—injury or damage);
subsection 33B(3) (compliance with permit conditions—injury or damage);
subsection 38F(1) (contravention of order to import hazardous waste—basic contravention);
subsection 38G(1) (contravention of order to import hazardous waste—injury or damage).
Without limiting subsection (1), the CEO may, under that subsection:
order the waste to be exported; or
specify the day on or before which anything required to be done in relation to the waste is to be done.
An order under this section may also require the person to give the CEO (by a specified time and in a specified manner) specified information relating to the dealing with the waste.

section.heading: Orders relating to export of hazardous waste

content.p: If a person contravenes one or more of the provisions mentioned in subsection (2) in relation to hazardous waste, the CEO may, in writing, order the person to deal with the waste in a specified way.
For the purposes of subsection (1), the provisions are the following:
subsection 33C(1) (export of hazardous waste—basic contravention);
subsection 33C(2) (export in accordance with permit—basic contravention);
subsection 33C(3) (compliance with permit conditions—basic contravention);
subsection 33D(1) (export of hazardous waste—injury or damage);
subsection 33D(2) (export in accordance with permit—injury or damage);
subsection 33D(3) (compliance with permit conditions—injury or damage).
Without limiting subsection (1), the CEO may, under that subsection:
order the waste to be imported; or
specify the day on or before which anything required to be done in relation to the waste is to be done.
An order under this section may also require the person to give the CEO (by a specified time and in a specified manner) specified information relating to the dealing with the waste.

section.heading: Orders relating to transit of hazardous waste

content.p: If a person contravenes one or more of the provisions mentioned in subsection (2) in relation to hazardous waste, the CEO may, in writing, order the person to deal with the waste in a specified way.
For the purposes of subsection (1), the provisions are the following:
subsection 33E(1) (transit of hazardous waste—basic contravention);
subsection 33E(2) (compliance with transit permit to bring waste into Australia—basic contravention);
subsection 33E(3) (compliance with transit permit to export waste—basic contravention);
subsection 33E(4) (compliance with transit permit conditions—basic contravention);
subsection 33F(1) (transit of hazardous waste—injury or damage);
subsection 33F(2) (compliance with transit permit to bring waste into Australia—injury or damage);
subsection 33F(3) (compliance with transit permit to export waste—injury or damage);
subsection 33F(4) (compliance with transit permit conditions—injury or damage).
Without limiting subsection (1), the CEO may, under that subsection:
order the waste to be exported; or
specify the day on or before which anything required to be done in relation to the waste is to be done.
An order under this section may also require the person to give the CEO (by a specified time and in a specified manner) specified information relating to the dealing with the waste.

section.heading: Orders to remedy or mitigate damage

content.p: If:
a person contravenes one or more of the following provisions in relation to hazardous waste:
subsection 33A(1), (2) or (3) (import of hazardous waste—basic contravention);
subsection 33B(1), (2) or (3) (import of hazardous waste—injury or damage);
subsection 33C(1), (2) or (3) (export of hazardous waste—basic contravention);
subsection 33D(1), (2) or (3) (export of hazardous waste—injury or damage);
subsection 33E(1), (2), (3) or (4) (transit of hazardous waste—basic contravention);
subsection 33F(1), (2), (3) or (4) (transit of hazardous waste—injury or damage); and
the CEO is satisfied that the contravention resulted in the waste causing significant injury or damage to human beings or the environment;
the CEO may, in writing, order the person to take such steps as the CEO thinks proper to remedy or mitigate the damage.
Without otherwise limiting subsection (1), the CEO must not, under that subsection, order the person to pay compensation.

section.heading: Orders authorising import of exported hazardous waste where it cannot be dealt with as intended

content.p: If:
a person has exported hazardous waste in accordance with the requirements of this Act; and
the waste cannot be dealt with in accordance with:
if the export was authorised by an export permit—the permit (including the permit conditions); or
if the export was ordered by the CEO under section 34—the order;
the person may apply to the CEO, in writing, for an order authorising the person to import the waste.
If the CEO receives an application under subsection (1), the CEO may make the order.
The CEO may, in the order, require that the waste be imported and dealt with in a specified way.
Without limiting subsection (3), the CEO may, under that subsection, specify the day on or before which anything required to be done in relation to the waste is to be done.
An order under this section may also require the person to give the CEO (by a specified time and in a specified manner) specified information relating to the dealing with the waste.

section.heading: Orders to remedy or mitigate damage if order under section 34, 35, 35A or 38 not complied with

content.p: If:
the person has been given an order under section 34, 35, 35A or 38 requiring the person:
to deal with hazardous waste in a specified way; or
to deal with hazardous waste by a specified time; and
the person does an act or omits to do an act; and
the act or omission contravenes the requirement; and
the CEO is satisfied that the non-compliance with the requirement resulted in the waste causing significant injury or damage to human beings or the environment;
the CEO may, in writing, order the person to take such steps as the CEO thinks proper to remedy or mitigate the damage.
Note: A requirement to deal with hazardous waste in a specified way includes a requirement to import or export the waste.
The CEO must not, under subsection (1), order the person to pay compensation.

section.heading: CEO may take action and recover costs if order under section 34, 35, 35A, 36, 38 or 38A not complied with

content.p: If:
the CEO makes an order under section 34, 35, 35A, 36, 38 or 38A requiring a person to do something; and
the person does not do the thing as and when required by the order;
the CEO may arrange for the thing to be done.

If the Commonwealth incurs costs because of arrangements made by the CEO under subsection (1), the person is liable to pay to the Commonwealth an amount equal to so much of those costs as are reasonable and the amount may be recovered by the Commonwealth as a debt due to the Commonwealth in:
the Court; or
the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia (Division 2); or
a court of a State or Territory that has jurisdiction in relation to the matter.

section.heading: Failure to deal with waste in contravention of order under section 34, 35 or 35A—basic contravention

content.p: Failure to deal with waste
A person contravenes this subsection if:
the person has been given an order under section 34, 35 or 35A requiring the person:
to deal with hazardous waste in a specified way; or
to deal with hazardous waste by a specified time; and
the person does an act or omits to do an act; and
the act or omission contravenes the requirement.
Note 1: The physical elements of an offence against subsection (2) are set out in this subsection (see section 58F).
Note 2: A requirement to deal with hazardous waste in a specified way includes a requirement to import or export the waste.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 5 years or 300 penalty units, or both.
Strict liability offence
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: 60 penalty units.
Civil penalty provision
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 600 penalty units.

section.heading: Failure to deal with waste in contravention of order under section 34, 35 or 35A—injury or damage to human beings or the environment

content.p: Failure to deal with waste
A person contravenes this subsection if:
the person has been given an order under section 34, 35 or 35A requiring the person:
to deal with hazardous waste in a specified way; or
to deal with hazardous waste by a specified time; and
the person does an act or omits to do an act; and
the act or omission contravenes the requirement; and
the non-compliance with the requirement injures or damages human beings or the environment.
Note 1: The physical elements of an offence against subsection (2) are set out in this subsection (see section 58F).
Note 2: A requirement to deal with hazardous waste in a specified way includes a requirement to import or export the waste.
Fault-based offence
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 8 years or 500 penalty units, or both.
Alternative verdict
In a trial for an offence against subsection (2), the trier of fact may find the defendant not guilty of that offence, but guilty of an offence against subsection 38C(2), if:
the trier of fact is not satisfied that the defendant is guilty of the offence against subsection (2) of this section; and
the trier of fact is satisfied that the defendant is guilty of the offence against subsection 38C(2); and
the defendant has been accorded procedural fairness in relation to that finding of guilt.
Strict liability offence
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: 60 penalty units.
Civil penalty provision
A person is liable to a civil penalty if the person contravenes subsection (1).
Civil penalty: 1,000 penalty units.
